sections.subtitle: Match context
sections.text: Bournemouth host Leeds United at the Vitality Stadium. Bournemouth are 9th (48 points), Leeds are 15th (39). Streaks point to a close game: Bournemouth are unbeaten in 12, Leeds are unbeaten in 6. The Sofascore model gives home win 40%, draw 26%, away win 34%, with both teams to score at 53%.

sections.subtitle: Current form
sections.text: Bournemouth are unbeaten in their last 5, including strong away wins at Arsenal and Newcastle, and have created steady xG across this run. Leeds have W2-D3 from their last 5, posted high chance creation (xG 2.82 vs Wolves, 2.57 at Manchester United, 3.09 at West Ham), and kept 3 clean sheets, though they conceded late at West Ham.

sections.subtitle: Head-to-head
sections.text: The last 2 meetings produced a draw at Elland Road and a decisive Bournemouth home win in 2023. Trends favour goals: both teams have scored in 6/7 and over 2.5 goals landed in 6/7. Bournemouth are without a clean sheet vs Leeds in 7.

sections.subtitle: Season stats and tendencies
sections.text: Bournemouth: 50 scored (rank 6), 50 conceded; total expected goals 54.16 (goals overperformance +4.16). They have 77 big chances (40% conversion), average possession 50%, 9 clean sheets, and 5.48 corners per game (rank 6). Late impact is notable (26% of goals on 76–90). Leeds: 42 scored, 49 conceded; late scoring is a feature (29% on 76–90).

sections.subtitle: Tactical and key players
sections.text: Bournemouth’s direct threat and transitions suit Eli Junior Kroupi (10 goals from 6.71 xG) with Alex Scott in strong recent form. Marcos Senesi’s distribution (high long-ball share) helps find runners. For Leeds, Noah Okafor is in form (goal contributions across recent games), Dominic Calvert-Lewin offers penalty-box presence, while Ethan Ampadu anchors midfield and Lucas Perri has excelled recently in goal.

sections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
sections.text: Referee Michael Salisbury averages 3.3 yellows and 0.20 reds per match. Bournemouth pick up 2.36 yellows per game and commit many fouls; recent head-to-heads have been low on cards. With Bournemouth averaging 5.48 corners per game and Leeds typically around 4–5 recently, expect about 10 corners and around 4 yellows overall.

sections.subtitle: Match prediction
sections.text: Margins look thin. Bournemouth’s longer unbeaten stretch and home edge are slightly offset by Leeds’ upturn in chance creation. Model lean is towards Bournemouth, with a moderate chance both teams score and a meaningful draw risk.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match context
halftimeSections.text: Goalless at the interval at Vitality Stadium, but Bournemouth have controlled most of the first half. They have sustained territory, more box entries and more efforts on target, while Leeds United have largely defended deep and looked to break. The home side’s pressure built towards half-time and they look the likelier to force the opener if they maintain this rhythm.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Attacking patterns and momentum
halftimeSections.text: Leeds United began with a brief front‑foot spell, but Bournemouth quickly took control and kept the initiative for long stretches. The home side enjoyed several strong attacking waves around the middle of the half and again just before the break, pinning Leeds United back. The visitors’ attacking moments were isolated, with only short counters and a late half-time response.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Key first-half stats
halftimeSections.text: Possession: Bournemouth 61–39. Shots on target: 2–1. Corners: 5–0. Expected goals: 0.35–0.03. Final third entries: 39–21. Penalty area entries: 35–8. Duels won: Bournemouth 39% vs Leeds United 61%. Aerial duels won: Bournemouth 39% vs Leeds United 61%. Notable defensive work for Leeds United came from Pascal Struijk (9 clearances) and Jaka Bijol (6), while for Bournemouth Ryan Christie registered 1 shot on target and Eli Junior Kroupi produced 2 key passes.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Tactical observations and adjustments
halftimeSections.text: Bournemouth are using width and quick switches to isolate full-backs, with overlapping runs creating low crosses and cut-backs. The final action has lacked precision, so sharper movements across the near post and late midfield runs could convert territory into clear chances. Set pieces look promising given the corner volume. Leeds United are compact in a low to mid block, relying on centre-backs to clear and on counters through Brenden Aaronson and runners from midfield. To relieve pressure, they need earlier support to the first receiver in transition and occasional higher starting positions for full-backs to contest second balls. If Bournemouth continue to dominate, a direct option into the striker and attacking the second phase around the box could be decisive.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Set-pieces, cards and corners
halftimeSections.text: Corners favour Bournemouth 5–0 and their deliveries have been consistent; they are likely to finish ahead on corner count, with most second‑half corners again for the home side. Discipline: Bournemouth have 2 yellow cards, Leeds United none. With Bournemouth pressing and Leeds United defending deep, another 1–2 bookings are plausible, with the next card slightly more likely for the home side. No red‑card signals so far.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Second-half outlook
halftimeSections.text: Bournemouth’s chance volume and territory edge suggest the opening goal is more likely to fall their way, especially if they sustain tempo early after the restart. Leeds United’s route back is through fast counters and set plays, but they need better retention on first passes out to threaten consistently. The next goal should shape the match strongly; if Bournemouth score first, their control should allow them to manage the game state.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match prediction
halftimeSections.text: Bournemouth to edge a tight contest. Prediction: Bournemouth 1–0 Leeds United. Next goal: Bournemouth. Most likely home scorer based on involvement and shot profile: Ryan Christie.
